job.title: HSEQ Advisor
job.description:

This organisation is a major player in construction materials, turning recovered waste into high specification products used across roads, rail and civil infrastructure projects. It operates as part of a global materials group with a genuine sustainability story behind what it produces. The safety function here is well established and highly regarded internally, backed by a business that offers real career pathways, structured leadership development and the ability to move across a much wider network of sites nationally.

ABOUT THE ROLE

HSEQ Advisor. Reports to the General Manager, transitioning to the National HSEQ Manager as the broader team is consolidated. No direct reports. This is a hands on, plant based role covering three core operational sites, replacing an advisor within an already well established function. The role exists to strengthen critical risk controls on the ground and be a genuine, trusted presence for plant teams day to day.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 
  • Provide expert HSEQ advice to staff and management across assigned sites
  • Deliver daily visible leadership activities including safety conversations, critical control checks and site walks
  • Assess whether critical risk controls are genuinely effective, not just present on paper
  • Lead and participate in incident investigations, recommending corrective actions
  • Support audits and inspections against the national auditing schedule
  • Deliver HSEQ training and awareness sessions
  • Assist with injury management and workers compensation cases
  • Contribute to the national HSEQ strategy and annual improvement plan
THE ESSENTIALS
  • Proven experience in a WHS or HSEQ role within a high risk industry
  • Strong understanding of critical risk management and control effectiveness
  • Working knowledge of environmental requirements, including dust and silica management
  • Working understanding of health requirements such as drug and alcohol testing and fitness for work programs
  • Familiarity with return to work and workers compensation processes
  • Comfortable spending the majority of your time on the plants rather than behind a desk
  • Full drivers licence

  • Fully maintained company vehicle

  • Backing of a global materials group with opportunities across sites nationally

  • Employee discounts, novated leasing and salary sacrifice options

job.title: HSE Resource - Governance, Systems and Compliance

HE COMPANY

This organisation is a major player in Australia's defence sector, supporting some of the nation's most critical capability programs. Backed by a global parent and shaped by recent growth and consolidation, the business is investing heavily in strengthening its safety and compliance foundations as it scales. It's a workplace where the work genuinely matters, where safety maturity is taken seriously at every level, and where the pace and pressure reflect the importance of what's being delivered.

THE ROLE

Reporting to the HSE Director, this is a hands on, individual contributor role with no direct reports, offered on an initial six month term with genuine potential to extend. The role exists to lead a complete rewrite of the organisation's EHS procedures and associated documentation, taking the current suite back to first principles and rebuilding it to align with both American and Australian standards. This means leading the end to end rewrite of procedures, standards, work instructions and supporting documentation, reviewing what currently exists and finding ways to simplify, standardise and modernise it, and translating technical and operational requirements into documentation people can actually use. It also involves facilitating consultation with operational teams, HSE professionals, subject matter experts and leadership through workshops, interviews and review sessions, owning the full document lifecycle from drafting through to consultation, review, approval, publication and periodic review, and coordinating document and version control so releases stay on schedule. The role supports internal and external audits relating to HSE systems and documentation, and requires ongoing monitoring of applicable HSE legislation and standards to keep everything current.

  • Own the full document lifecycle, from drafting through consultation, review, approval, publication and periodic review
  • Coordinate document and version control, tracking review comments, actions and approvals to keep releases on schedule
  • Support internal and external audits relating to HSE systems and documentation
  • Monitor applicable HSE legislation and standards, ensuring documentation reflects current obligations and best practice
THE ESSENTIALS

This is one of Australia's largest and longest standing construction materials businesses, with operations covering quarrying, cement, concrete, asphalt, bitumen and recycling across the country. Safety here isn't a policy binder on a shelf, it's built into how leaders are expected to operate day to day, with a values framework that puts people ahead of production and a genuine track record of investing in the people who hold that line. This is a business where a safety professional gets heard in the room, not just consulted after the fact.

This is a Health and Safety Business Partner position, reporting to the Head of Business Partnering Health and Safety, based in Tasmania with regular travel to South Australia. There are no direct reports, so this is not a people leadership role.The purpose is to give site leaders and teams the strategic safety guidance and hands on support they need to make Zero Harm a lived reality rather than a slogan.

Day to day, you will be coaching and influencing leaders and employees to lift safety culture, partnering with site leadership to drive consistent implementation of HSEQ management systems and safe systems of work, and leading incident investigations, audits and corrective actions through to genuine close out.   • Partner with site leadership to drive consistent implementation of HSEQ management systems and safe systems of work

  • Deliver HSE training and communications across your sites
  • Maintain and monitor site risk registers with key stakeholders
  • Support injury management, RTW and occupational hygiene activity alongside specialist teams
  • Contribute risk perspective into capital and operational budget planning
  • Report to HSE and Operational Leadership on progress and performance

  • Minimum 5 years in health and safety within resources, construction or energy sectors

This role will have a strong focus on evacuation planning, emergency response procedures, exercising and employee training, ensuring people are well prepared to respond effectively to a range of emergency scenarios.

  • Provide guidance and support to employees and leaders regarding emergency response procedures, evacuation requirements and emergency roles and responsibilities.
  • Support the development and maintenance of Business Continuity and Emergency Management programs.
  • Review emergency management documentation, procedures and processes to ensure they remain current, practical and fit for purpose.
  • Assess emergency management capability and provide reports and recommendations to address identified gaps.
  • Coordinate emergency response activities and provide support during incidents and exercises where required.
  • Work collaboratively with stakeholders to promote a positive emergency preparedness and safety culture.
  • Maintain awareness of relevant legislation, standards and contemporary emergency management practices.
Essential Experience & Criteria
  • Relevant experience in emergency management, emergency planning, business continuity, risk management or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and reviewing evacuation and emergency response plans.
  • Proven experience delivering emergency management and evacuation training to employees and/or emergency response teams.
  • Experience developing and facilitating emergency exercises, drills and simulations.
  • Strong understanding of emergency management principles, risk assessment and organisational preparedness.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively across all levels of an organisation.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to develop clear plans, procedures, reports and training materials.
  • Ability to identify gaps in emergency preparedness and develop practical, achievable recommendations.

job.title: HSE System Improvement & Reporting
job.description:
THE COMPANY

This organisation owns and operates the high voltage transmission infrastructure that powers South Australia, sitting at the centre of one of the most renewables-intensive electricity systems in the world. With a capital works pipeline approaching $4 billion and projects currently reshaping how the state generates and moves energy, this is a business with genuine momentum behind it. The culture is collaborative, the engagement scores are high, and the people here consistently describe meaningful work and strong leadership. For someone who wants their contribution to matter, this is that kind of place.

THE ROLE

This is not a traditional safety role and it is not being advertised as one. This organisation has reached a point in its safety maturity where data, systems and governance are as important as boots on the ground, and they need someone who gets that.

The systems environment is well established and in good shape, but there is real work to do. Some areas are more manual than they should be, some reporting is more complex than it needs to be, and the narrative being delivered to leadership could be sharper. This person's job is to fix that, to own the data, govern it properly, and turn it into something the Board and Executive Management Team can actually act on.

If you have spent your HSE career gravitating toward the systems and data side of the profession, if you get frustrated when platforms do not talk to each other or when good data produces mediocre reporting, this role was written for you.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Lead the optimisation and integration of HSE management systems aligned to ISO 45001 and ISO 14001
  • Own HSE data governance frameworks including data ownership, quality, definitions and metrics
  • Collect, validate and analyse HSE and risk data across multiple systems to identify trends, anomalies and gaps
  • Translate complex HSE data into clear, compelling narratives for non-technical audiences including the Executive Management Team and Board
  • Deliver recurring reporting packs, trend analysis and critical control verification reporting for Divisional Leadership Teams
  • Champion automation and AI-enabled ways of working across the HSE function
  • Drive continuous improvement of reporting cadence, format and content in line with stakeholder needs
THE ESSENTIALS
  • Proven experience within HSE systems, analytics, digital improvement or related roles in high-risk industries
  • Demonstrated experience building or improving data governance frameworks and digital HSE workflows
  • Strong Power BI and Excel capability
  • Experience with HSE management systems such as SAP EHS, Intelex or equivalent
  • Solid understanding of HSE metrics including TRIFR, LTIFR, leading and lagging indicators and assurance models including ISO 45001, ISO 14001 and ISO 31000
  • Ability to prepare Board and executive level materials and communicate findings clearly to non-technical audiences
  • Background in construction, electrical, heavy industry, utilities or mining strongly preferred
THE BENEFITS
  • Five weeks annual leave
  • 16 weeks paid parental leave
  • Hybrid working, three days in the office and two from home with flexible start times
  • Pool vehicles for all site travel
  • Generous and achievable bonuses
  • Endorsed Work180 employer
